clean_story:
Memory refinement. Nighttime director.

The term comes from how sleep actively reshapes what the brain remembers, like a film editor cutting raw footage into a coherent story. During deep sleep, the brain replays the day’s events at high speed, strengthening important memories and trimming away the irrelevant. It’s not passive storage—it’s selective curation. For example, students who sleep after learning a new skill retain it better than those who stay awake, as sleep consolidates the neural pathways. Meanwhile, emotional memories often get amplified, while trivial details fade. This editing happens in precise waves: slow oscillations coordinate spikes of activity that transfer memories from the hippocampus to long-term storage in the cortex. Without this process, the mind would be cluttered with noise. Three related subjects are memory consolidation, dream mechanisms and neural plasticity.
